title: COLLAPSE UNDER LOAD now covers what was actually felling them
question: With it OFF, does the bed read as a stand that got to grow up -- or as plants glued together in ways that look wrong?
context_md:
You were right: the switch was wired, but it was scoped to the wrong rules.

`snapped under load` reads a flat **0** on the lab bed -- the two rules the
switch covered never fire in there at all, so it had nothing to turn off. What
was actually taking your trees down is the support check: a plant that has no
anchorage in soil marks its own cells "unreached", schedules its own structural
check, and is felled whole -- pieces of up to 75 cells, the entire organism,
with zero anchors left in it. Nothing had touched them.

The switch now covers that too, for LIVING plants only. Dead wood still comes
apart, so culling and rot still clear the box, and the axe still works
outdoors.

Same binary, same bed, 8 founders / 1 colony / 20,000 frames, switched at run
time:

                          ON            OFF
  severed by the check    683           31
  ...of them ALIVE        654           0
  standing plant cells    1,935         2,923
  standing flower/fruit   0 / 1         8 / 11
  rotted                  927           1,025

The flower and fruit row is the one I would look at: plants that stop being
demolished mid-life get far enough to reproduce.

The underlying defect is filed (open-bugs-handoff §B2) and not fixed -- this is
a control in your hand, not a repair. With the switch ON it is exactly as live
as it was.

items.label: switch ON (shipped): 654 living cells severed, 1,935 standing
switch OFF (this change): 0 living cells severed, 2,923 standing
